facts.statement: Paludititan was a titanosaurian sauropod that lived in present-day Romania during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Paludititan is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur which lived in the area of present Romania during the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Paludititan lived on the island ecosystem known as Hațeg Island.
facts.quote: It existed in the island ecosystem known as Hațeg Island.

facts.statement: At the time of its discovery, the skeleton was the most complete sauropod skeleton ever found in Romania.
facts.quote: It was at the time the most complete sauropod skeleton ever discovered in Romania.

facts.statement: The species Paludititan nalatzensis was named and described in 2010 by Zoltán Csiki, Vlad Codrea, Cătălin Jipa-Murzea, and Pascal Godefroit.
facts.quote: In 2010, the type species Paludititan nalatzensis was named and described by Zoltán Csiki, Vlad Codrea, Cătălin Jipa-Murzea and Pascal Godefroit.

facts.statement: The specific name nalatzensis refers to the fossil's discovery location, Nălațvad.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to its finding place Nălațvad.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found in the Hațeg Basin within the Sânpetru Formation, dating to the early Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: The holotype, UBB NVM1, was found in the Hațeg Basin, in a silty mudstone layer of the Sânpetru Formation, dating from the early Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: The holotype is a partial skeleton lacking the skull but includes dorsal vertebrae, tail vertebrae, chevrons, parts of the pelvis, a femur fragment, and toe claws.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial skeleton lacking the skull. It contains three dorsal vertebrae, at least nine caudal vertebrae, twelve chevrons, the right half of the pelvis, a left ischium, the lower end of the right thighbone, and two toe claws.

facts.statement: Although the remains were not articulated, their close association suggests they belong to a single individual.
facts.quote: The remains were not found in articulation but in such close association that it is likely they represent a single individual.

facts.statement: Researchers initially considered the possibility that the skeleton belonged to Magyarosaurus dacus, a contemporary sauropod from the same habitat.
facts.quote: The describing authors of Paludititan considered the possibility that the skeleton was a specimen of Magyarosaurus dacus, a coeval titanosaurian sauropod sharing the same habitat.

facts.statement: Paludititan possessed unique features in its back vertebrae where certain ridges ran parallel instead of touching.
facts.quote: In the rear vertebrae of the back, the top of the lamina centrodiapophysealis anterior, the front ridge on the underside of the lateral process, obliquely curving to the front and above runs parallel to the top of the lamina centrodiapophysealis posterior, the rear ridge, instead of touching it.

facts.statement: The ischium peduncle featured a conspicuous triangular process forming a buttress that overlapped the ilium.
facts.quote: The peduncle of the ischium, touching the ilium, has a conspicuous triangular process at the outer upper rear, forming a buttress that overlaps the ischial pedicel of the ilium.

facts.statement: A feature once thought unique to Paludititan was later found in other vertebrae, so it is no longer considered an autapomorphy.
facts.quote: When the species was described, the paleontologists are believed that this feature is autapomorphic for Paludititan, however, some vertebrae found in 2019 in the vicinity of a village called Valiora, found to certainly not belong to Paludititan, also show this feature, so it can no longer be considered as an autapomorphy of Paludititan.

facts.statement: Paludititan was classified within the Titanosauria in 2010.
facts.quote: Paludititan was placed in 2010 in the Titanosauria.

facts.statement: Paludititan was considered a probable member of the Lithostrotia clade.
facts.quote: More precisely, it was considered a probable member of the Lithostrotia.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis suggested Paludititan was a sister species to the South American dinosaur Epachthosaurus.
facts.quote: Cladistic analysis suggested it was a sister species of the South American Epachthosaurus.

facts.statement: A 2019 study described Paludititan as a member of the Saltasauridae family.
facts.quote: In the same year, Gorscak & O'Connor (2019) in their description of Mnyamawamtuka recovered Paludititan as a saltasaurid.

facts.statement: Paludititan lived alongside other island dwarf dinosaurs including Magyarosaurus, Telmatosaurus, and Zalmoxes on Hațeg Island.
facts.quote: Paludititan lived on the Cretaceous Hațeg Island with a diverse assemblage of animals, including other island dwarfs such as its relative Magyarosaurus, the hadrosaurid Telmatosaurus and the iguanodontian Zalmoxes.

facts.statement: The island ecosystem included endemic dinosaurs such as the nodosaurid Struthiosaurus and the avialan Balaur.
facts.quote: Other endemic dinosaurs include the nodosaurid Struthiosaurus, several small, fragmentary maniraptorans Bradycneme, Elopteryx, Heptasteornis, and the avialan Balaur.

facts.statement: The top predator of the Hațeg Island ecosystem was the giant pterosaur Hatzegopteryx.
facts.quote: The top predator of the island ecosystem was the giant azhdarchid pterosaur Hatzegopteryx.

facts.statement: Paludititan was a small sauropod with a shoulder height of about 2 meters.
facts.quote: Paludititan era un miembro pequeño de los Sauropoda, con una altura de hombros de unos 2 m.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Paludititan's length at 6 meters and weight at one ton in 2016.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul en 2016 estimó la longitud de Magyarosaurus dacus y Paludititan, considerado por él como un posible taxón único, en 6 metros, el peso en una tonelada.

facts.statement: Paludititan was described in 2010 based on partial skeletal remains found in the Hațeg Basin in present-day Romania.
facts.quote: Fue descrito en 2010 por Zoltan Csikiego et al. basados en un esqueleto parcial, incluidas partes de la columna vertebral y la cintura escapular, descubiertas en los estratos de la Cuenca Haţeg Nǎlaţ-Vad, en Transilvania, en la actual Rumania.

facts.statement: The remains were found in such close association that they likely represent a single individual.
facts.quote: Los restos no se encontraron articulados sino en una asociación tan estrecha que es probable que representen a un solo individuo.

facts.statement: The authors considered the possibility that the skeleton was a specimen of Magyarosaurus dacus, a contemporary sauropod from the same habitat.
facts.quote: Los autores que describen Paludititan consideraron la posibilidad de que el esqueleto fuera un espécimen de Magyarosaurus dacus, un saurópodo titanosaurio coetáneo que comparte el mismo hábitat.

facts.statement: The authors felt justified in naming a separate taxon pending further discoveries.
facts.quote: Se sintieron justificados para nombrar un taxón separado, en espera de nuevos descubrimientos.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis indicates Paludititan is a relatively advanced titanosaurian, though its closest relatives remain unclear.
facts.quote: Una evaluación por parte de los autores mediante un análisis filogenético indica que Paludititan es un relativamente avanzado titanosáurido, pero sus parientes más cercanos no están claros.

facts.statement: Paludititan was placed in the Titanosauria in 2010.
facts.quote: Paludititan se colocó en 2010 en el Titanosauria .

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis suggested Paludititan was a sister species to the South American Epachthosaurus.
facts.quote: El análisis cladístico sugirió que era una especie hermana del Epachthosaurus sudamericano.

facts.statement: Paludititan lived on the Cretaceous Hațeg Island alongside other dwarf animals such as its relative Magyarosaurus, the hadrosaurid Telmatosaurus, and the iguanodontian Zalmoxes.
facts.quote: Paludititan vivió en la isla Cretácica Hațeg con un conjunto diverso de animales, incluyendo otros animales enanos como su pariente Magyarosaurus, el hadrosáurido Telmatosaurus y el iguanodontiano Zalmoxes.

facts.statement: The main predator of the island ecosystem was the giant azdarchid pterosaur Hatzegopteryx.
facts.quote: El principal depredador del ecosistema de la isla fue el pterosaurio azdárquido gigante Hatzegopteryx.

facts.statement: Paludititan belongs to the parent group Eutitanosauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Eutitanosauria

facts.statement: Paludititan is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Paludititan lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Paludititan was named by Csiki and colleagues in 2010.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Paludititan (genus), Csiki et al. 2010

facts.statement: There are currently two recorded fossil occurrences of Paludititan.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 2
